subsystems.name: Probe mesh
subsystems.role: ultra-thin, flexible polymer filaments carrying electrodes that move with the brain instead of cutting it.
parts: electrode sites of gold, platinum or titanium nitride

subsystems.name: Delivery system
subsystems.role: gets the fragile mesh through the skull and into the target millimetres of cortex without buckling.

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: amplifies and digitises hundreds to thousands of weak neural signals at once.

subsystems.name: Tissue interface
subsystems.role: keeps the electrodes close to neurons and the immune response quiet.

subsystems.name: Decoding and control
subsystems.role: turns spike and local-field patterns into intent, and stimulation into sensation.

buildSteps.title: Design the mesh
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose electrode spacing, filament width and bending stiffness so the mesh matches the elasticity of brain tissue rather than that of a needle.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate on a wafer
buildSteps.detail: Photolithography builds the mesh flat: polymer is spun on a carrier wafer, metal traces and electrode sites are deposited and patterned, then another polymer layer encapsulates them.

buildSteps.title: Release the mesh
buildSteps.detail: The sacrificial layer under the device is etched away, leaving a free-standing, flexible mesh or a single thread.

buildSteps.title: Functionalise the surface
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes are coated to lower impedance and reduce scarring, and the polymer is cleaned and checked for biocompatibility.

buildSteps.title: Build the headstage
buildSteps.detail: The recording chip, wireless link and power coil are assembled into a sealed package that sits on the skull or under the scalp.

buildSteps.title: Sterilise and load
buildSteps.detail: The mesh is loaded into a thin needle or onto a stiff shuttle under sterile conditions.

buildSteps.title: Implant
buildSteps.detail: Through a small craniotomy, the needle or robotic inserter places the mesh at the target depth; the shuttle is withdrawn and the mesh relaxes into the tissue.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and record
buildSteps.detail: Over days to weeks the tissue settles around the electrodes; signals are acquired, and decoding software is calibrated to the individual.

prerequisites.why: they must carry current for years in warm, salty tissue without cracking or dissolving.
mesh electronics have been injected into animal brains; doing it repeatably and safely in people is not routine.
thousands of electrodes need on-implant multiplexing and wireless telemetry that do not overheat tissue.
scar tissue forming around any implant slowly silences recordings; a 10-year interface is unproven.
speech and cursor control have been demonstrated in small human trials, but decoders still need frequent recalibration.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials using stiff microelectrode arrays and an endovascular electrode, restoring cursor control and basic speech
pathway.unlocks: proof that decoded neural signals can be useful to paralysed patients.

pathway.milestone: wireless implants with roughly a thousand channels and no cable through the skin
injectable polymer meshes in first human studies
pathway.unlocks: far higher electrode density with less surgical trauma.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional, long-lived interfaces with sensory feedback
pathway.unlocks: paralysis recovery that feels natural, and — if safety holds — cognitive augmentation.
